info.title: NaN API
info.description:
Open models on a shared EU inference cluster. Zero logs.

The NaN API is OpenAI-compatible: predictable, resource-oriented URLs, JSON request and response bodies, and standard HTTP verbs and status codes. Point any OpenAI SDK at our base URL and your existing code keeps working. Change the base URL and the API key, and that's it.

One schema across every model, so you only learn the API once. Change the `model` field to switch models; everything else stays the same.

- Base URL: `https://api.nan.builders/v1`
- OpenAPI spec: this document. Import it into Postman, Insomnia, or your own tooling.

If you use the [Helmcode](https://helmcode.com) enterprise service, the base URL is `https://api.helmcode.com/v1` instead. Every other endpoint is identical.

## Authentication

Every inference request authenticates with an API key, sent as a Bearer token:

```
Authorization: Bearer $NAN_API_KEY
```

You must be a NaN community member. Generate your key from user settings, under "API Keys", on the [platform](https://cloud.nan.builders/). The key is personal and non-transferable. Keep it secret: never embed one in client-side code or commit it to source control. Requests must go over HTTPS; calls over plain HTTP fail.

### Platform tokens

For scripts that only manage [Runs](#tag/runs), [Automations](#tag/automations), [Secrets](#tag/secrets), [Notifications](#tag/notifications) and [Approvals](#tag/approvals), and list your [Workspaces](#tag/workspaces), create a **platform token** (`nan_pat_...`) under "Tokens" in your settings, and send it the same way: `Authorization: Bearer $NAN_TOKEN`. An API key works on inference and on Runs, Approvals, Workspaces and reading and running Automations; never on Secrets, Notifications or changes to automations. Each endpoint lists the credentials it accepts.

A platform token carries **scopes**, and each endpoint names the one it needs: `runs` (runs and approvals), `workspaces:read`, `automations:read` (read automations, templates, triggers and deliveries), `automations:run` (run an existing automation), `automations:write` (create, change and delete automations and their triggers), `secrets:read` (read secret metadata, never values), `secrets:write` (create, replace, change and delete secrets), `notifications:read` (read notification channels and their deliveries, never their URLs) and `notifications:write` (create, change, test and delete notification channels, and rotate their signing secrets). Scopes are independent: `secrets:write` does not include `secrets:read`, and `notifications:write` does not include `notifications:read`. New tokens get `runs` and `workspaces:read`. A token without the scope gets `403`:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "This platform token does not have the \"automations:run\" scope this endpoint requires. Create a token with that scope in the Tokens section of Settings at cloud.nan.builders.",
    "type": "permission_error",
    "param": null,
    "code": "token_scope_denied"
  }
}
```

A platform token never works for inference: the model endpoints answer `401`:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "Platform tokens (nan_pat_) cannot be used for inference. Use an inference API key (sk-) instead. Platform tokens only work on the platform API (/v1/runs, /v1/automations, /v1/approvals, /v1/secrets, /v1/notification-channels and GET /api/workspaces).",
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "param": null,
    "code": "token_not_valid_for_inference"
  }
}
```

### CLI session and the write scopes

Your secrets and your automations (with their triggers) can be managed through the API and the [NaN CLI](https://nan.builders/docs/nan-cli) where the write API is available for your account (it is being opened gradually). Three credentials can change them: you signed in at [cloud.nan.builders](https://cloud.nan.builders/), the **CLI session** that `nan auth login` saves, and a platform token with `automations:write` or `secrets:write`. Secret metadata is read with a CLI session or `secrets:read`. API keys (`sk-...`), the key inside a workspace and sessions from older clients are refused:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "This endpoint needs a browser session, a CLI session (nan auth login) or a platform token with the \"secrets:write\" scope. API keys (sk-), workspace keys and sessions from older clients are not accepted here: sign in again with the CLI or at cloud.nan.builders.",
    "type": "permission_error",
    "param": null,
    "code": "credential_not_allowed"
  }
}
```

A token with `secrets:write` lets whoever holds it replace any of your secrets. A token with `automations:write` lets whoever holds it create or change an automation that receives any of your secrets, with instructions of their choice and nothing waiting for approval: that is as good as reading every secret you have. Such a token, held by an agent or a script, can change your secrets or automations. These scopes can only be added to a token in the portal, signed in through your browser. The same goes for `notifications:read` and `notifications:write`, offered only where your account has notifications and the write API: a token with `notifications:write` decides where your notifications go. Give a token only the scopes its job needs, and run `nan auth login` on your own machine, never inside a workspace: the agents there could read the session.

### Browser sign-in

Some actions need you signed in through your browser at [cloud.nan.builders](https://cloud.nan.builders/), and no API key, platform token or CLI session can do them: approving a run, and creating a token with an `automations:`, `secrets:` or `notifications:` scope. Where the write API is not yet available for your account, changing automations and their triggers is also browser-only. Through the API they answer `403`:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "This action needs a browser session: sign in at cloud.nan.builders in your browser and try again from there. CLI sessions, API keys and platform tokens cannot approve runs or create tokens with automations or secrets scopes.",
    "type": "permission_error",
    "param": null,
    "code": "browser_session_required"
  }
}
```

## Making requests

The API is OpenAI-compatible, so point an official OpenAI SDK at our base URL and change nothing else:

```python
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key="$NAN_API_KEY",
    base_url="https://api.nan.builders/v1",
)

resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="deepseek-v4-flash",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
)
print(resp.choices[0].message.content)
```

## Streaming

Chat responses can stream token-by-token. Set `"stream": true` on `/chat/completions` and the response arrives as Server-Sent Events: each event is a `data:` line carrying a `chat.completion.chunk`, with the new text in `choices[0].delta.content`. A final `data: [DONE]` line ends the stream. `/chat/completions` streams incrementally on every chat model. `/responses` streams incrementally on `deepseek-v4-flash`, `glm5.3-flash`, `qwen3.8-flash`, `mimo-v2.6-flash` and `glm5.3`; on `qwen3.6` and `gemma4` it holds the whole answer and sends it in one burst at the end.

## Reasoning

Every chat model in the catalogue reasons before it answers, and one parameter controls it on every model in the catalogue, the same on both hosts: `reasoning_effort` on `/chat/completions`, `reasoning.effort` on `/responses`. The values are `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh` and `max`.

To turn reasoning off, send `"reasoning_effort": "none"` (or `"reasoning": {"effort": "none"}` on `/responses`). `glm5.3` and `glm5.3-flash` always reason and cannot stop: there `none` is applied as `minimal`, their shortest reasoning.

The switches other providers document are accepted too and mean exactly `none`: `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}`, `reasoning: {"enabled": false}`, `enable_thinking: false` and `chat_template_kwargs: {"enable_thinking": false}`, at the top level or inside `extra_body`. If a request carries both a value and one of these, the value wins. Any other value is passed through unchanged and is not part of this contract: depending on the model it is rejected with a `400` or ignored. Models outside the catalogue take `reasoning_effort` as their own API defines it, without these aliases.

What each value does per model: [Controlling reasoning](https://nan.builders/docs/models#controlling-reasoning).

## Rate limits

{{RATE_LIMITS}}

Image endpoints run on their own budget, separate from the model endpoints: 20 requests per minute and 100 requests per month. The usage endpoint is metered separately too: {{USAGE_RATE_LIMIT}} requests per minute per member. Exceed any limit and you get a `429`.

## Errors

NaN uses conventional HTTP status codes: `2xx` on success, `4xx` for a problem with the request (a missing parameter, an invalid key, an unavailable model) and `5xx` for a server-side error. Every error returns a JSON body in the OpenAI shape:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "message": "The model 'foo' does not exist.",
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "param": "model",
    "code": "model_not_found"
  }
}
```

`message` is human-readable, `param` names the offending field when applicable, and `code` is a short machine-readable string you can branch on.

| Status | Meaning | `code` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `400` | Invalid or malformed parameter (`param` says which); content blocked by the safety filter; a `max_tokens` above what the model can generate (a generic "Invalid request" message today); or a request that does not fit the model's context window. On the models hosted on the cluster (`qwen3.6`, `gemma4`) the overflow message is "Context length exceeded for model '...'" with the model's limit; on the other models it is usually that text, but it can arrive as the generic "Invalid request. Check your request parameters." | `"400"` (with `type: invalid_request_error`) · `content_policy_violation` |
| `401` | Missing or invalid API key, or a key whose tier does not reach the requested model (`glm5.3`): "This API key does not have access to the requested model", `type: auth_error`. Measured 2026-09-12. A platform token (`nan_pat_...`) sent to an inference endpoint answers `token_not_valid_for_inference`. | `invalid_api_key` · `token_not_valid_for_inference` |
| `402` | The token allowance is spent on a model that carries one. Not retryable: the counter returns to zero when that model's quota period does, the calendar month for the models counted per month and your billing period for `glm5.3`. | `monthly_cap_reached` |
| `403` | Your tier can't access this endpoint. Image generation requires inference membership. A model your tier cannot reach answers `401`, not this. On the platform endpoints: a platform token without the scope the endpoint needs, a credential that cannot change secrets or automations (see [CLI session and the write scopes](#description/cli-session-and-the-write-scopes)), or an action that needs a [browser sign-in](#description/browser-sign-in). | `tier_restricted` · `token_scope_denied` · `credential_not_allowed` · `browser_session_required` |
| `404` | The requested model doesn't exist. | `model_not_found` |
| `429` | Rate limit hit (`rpm_limit`, `max_parallel_requests`), the rolling 4h token budget of `glm5.3`, or a quota exhausted. | `rate_limit_exceeded` · `insufficient_quota` · `quota_exceeded` |
| `500` | Something went wrong on our side (includes upstream model errors). | (none) |
| `524` | Timeout, typical with large audio files on `/audio/transcriptions`. | (none) |

Retry `429` and `5xx` responses with exponential backoff. Don't retry `400`, `401`, `403`, or `404` blindly (a context overflow is not retried automatically either: shorten the input or pick a model with a larger window): they'll fail the same way every time until you change the request. `402` cannot be fixed by repetition either: it clears when that model's quota period resets.

## Model catalog

Every endpoint takes a `model` id. Capabilities vary by model:

| Model | Use for | Capabilities |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `deepseek-v4-flash` | Chat, vision, reasoning | Streaming, tool calling, reasoning, image input, 1M-token context. 3B tokens/month per member |
| `mimo-v2.6-flash` | Chat, vision, audio | Streaming, tool calling, reasoning, image input, audio input, 1M-token context. 1.0B tokens/month per member |
| `qwen3.8-flash` | Chat, vision, agents | Streaming, tool calling, reasoning (on by default), vision, 1M-token context. 500M tokens/month per member |
| `glm5.3-flash` | Chat, vision, agents | Streaming, tool calling, reasoning, vision, 1M-token context. 2B tokens/month per member |
| `qwen3.6` | Chat, agents | Streaming, tool calling, vision, reasoning (on by default; `reasoning_effort: "none"` turns it off) |
| `gemma4` | Chat, vision, agents | Streaming, tool calling, vision, reasoning (on by default; `reasoning_effort: "none"` turns it off) |
| `glm5.3` | Coding, long-horizon agents | Streaming, tool calling, reasoning trace, image, audio and video input, 1M-token context. Premium tier only |
| `qwen3-embedding` | Embeddings | 4096-dimension vectors |
| `rerank` | RAG reranking | Qwen3-Reranker-8B, 100+ languages |
| `kokoro` | Text-to-speech | Multiple voices and audio formats |
| `whisper` | Speech-to-text | Transcription with word/segment timestamps |
| `flux-2-klein` | Image generation | Text-to-image and image-to-image |
| `qwen-image-2.1` | Image generation (text→image) | 512-1280 px, 1-4 per request, seed 0-2147483647. 100 images/month per member (shared pool with flux-2-klein) |

`glm5.3` is served only to keys on the GLM 5.3 premium tier; every other model is available to any inference member. Call [List models](#tag/Models) for the exact set available to your key.

## Versioning & compatibility

The API tracks the OpenAI API surface, so OpenAI SDKs and tools work against `https://api.nan.builders/v1` unchanged. This reference documents the stable public `/v1` endpoints, plus the two read-only [Workspaces](#tag/workspaces) endpoints under `/api/workspaces`, and we add capabilities without breaking existing fields.

tags.name: Chat
tags.description: Chat completions, the main conversational endpoint.

tags.name: Runs
tags.description: Give an agent (Pi, Pi + Gentle Shell or Hermes) a task inside one of your workspaces and follow it. A run keeps going if the client disconnects. Accepts a member API key or a platform token with the `runs` scope. Guide: [Agent runs](https://nan.builders/docs/runs). Runs can use NaN inference or your own provider key: [Use your own provider key](https://nan.builders/docs/runs#use-your-own-provider-key-byok).

tags.name: Automations
tags.description: Your automations: saved agent tasks that webhooks, schedules or your own calls start. Reading needs a platform token with `automations:read`, running one `automations:run` (or your API key). Creating, changing and deleting automations and their triggers needs a CLI session (`nan auth login`) or a platform token with `automations:write`; API keys (`sk-...`) cannot. Where the write API is not yet available for your account, those routes answer `403 browser_session_required` and you make the change in the portal. Approving stays in the portal. Webhooks themselves arrive at `https://api.nan.builders/hooks/<token>`, signed by the sender. Guides: [Automations](https://nan.builders/docs/automations), [Webhooks and schedules](https://nan.builders/docs/webhooks).

tags.name: Secrets
tags.description: The tokens and keys your automations receive, and your own provider keys. The API never returns a value: it lists metadata, creates secrets, replaces values, changes descriptions and base URLs, and deletes. Reading needs a CLI session (`nan auth login`) or a platform token with `secrets:read`; writing, a CLI session or a token with `secrets:write`. API keys (`sk-...`) never read or write secrets. Where the write API is not yet available for your account, these routes answer `404`. Guide: [Secrets](https://nan.builders/docs/secrets).

tags.name: Notifications
tags.description: Notification channels: Slack, Microsoft Teams, Discord or your own HTTPS endpoint, told when an automation run waits for approval (`approval.pending`), fails or times out (`run.failed`), finishes (`run.finished`, opt-in), when an automation is switched off (`automation.disabled`) or its webhook keeps failing (`trigger.failing`). A channel URL is a credential: write-only, never returned (only `url_hint`). An `https` channel's signing secret is returned once, by create and by rotate. Reading needs a CLI session (`nan auth login`) or a platform token with `notifications:read`; changing, a CLI session or a token with `notifications:write`. API keys (`sk-...`) never read or change channels. Where notifications or the write API are not yet available for your account, these routes answer `404`. Payloads, signatures, digests and limits: [Notifications](https://nan.builders/docs/notifications).

tags.name: Approvals
tags.description: The actions your automation runs propose, and the ones waiting for your approval. List them, read a proposal and its diff, and reject. Approving is done only in the portal, signed in through your browser (`POST /v1/runs/{id}/approve` answers `403 browser_session_required` to API keys and platform tokens), so nothing a script or an agent holds can approve. Guide: [Automations](https://nan.builders/docs/automations#approve-or-reject-a-proposal).

tags.name: Workspaces
tags.description: Read-only access to your own workspaces, for scripts that need a workspace's name, id or status. Served at `https://api.nan.builders/api/workspaces`, outside `/v1`, to bearer credentials only (no cookies, no browser CORS). Creating, starting, stopping and deleting workspaces is done from the platform, not from this API. Guide: [Workspaces](https://nan.builders/docs/workspaces).

post.description: Creates a model response for the given chat conversation. Compatible with OpenAI's Chat Completions API.

model.description:
Model id. See [List models](#tag/Models) for what your key can use. Chat models are `deepseek-v4-flash`, `mimo-v2.6-flash`, `qwen3.8-flash`, `glm5.3-flash`, `qwen3.6`, `gemma4` and `glm5.3`.

`glm5.3` requires a key on the GLM 5.3 premium tier; other keys get `401` `auth_error` ("This API key does not have access to the requested model"), and do not see it in [List models](#tag/Models) either. The rest are available to every inference member.

messages.description: The conversation so far, oldest first. `content` is a string, or an array of parts (`text` + `image_url`) for vision input on every chat model: `deepseek-v4-flash`, `mimo-v2.6-flash`, `qwen3.8-flash`, `glm5.3-flash`, `qwen3.6`, `gemma4` and `glm5.3`.

max_tokens.description: Maximum number of tokens to generate. A value above what the model can generate is rejected with a generic `400`, except on `glm5.3-flash` and `deepseek-v4-flash` (see below). A request that does not fit the model's context window is rejected with a `400`: "Context length exceeded for model '...'" on `qwen3.6` and `gemma4`, usually the same text (sometimes the generic "Invalid request") on the other models. The value is used exactly as sent, with reasoning on or off, except above the model's maximum on two models, where it is lowered to that maximum: 131072 on `glm5.3-flash`, 393216 on `deepseek-v4-flash`. Reasoning tokens count inside it: with reasoning on, a small value can be spent entirely on reasoning, and the answer comes back with an empty `content` and `finish_reason: "length"` (the reasoning is in `message.reasoning_content`, and `usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens` equals `completion_tokens`); non-streamed calls also carry the `x-nan-truncated-in-reasoning: true` response header. Turn reasoning off (`reasoning_effort: "none"`) for a reliable fix (GLM cannot turn it off; `minimal` is its shortest); a lower effort is a hint, not a cap, on `deepseek-v4-flash` and `qwen3.8-flash`. Or send a generous value and use `stream: true`.

temperature.description: Sampling temperature. Higher is more random, lower more deterministic.

top_p.description: Nucleus sampling: only consider the top `top_p` probability mass.

stream.description: When `true`, the reply arrives as Server-Sent Events: each `data:` line is a `chat.completion.chunk` with new text in `choices[0].delta.content`, ending with `data: [DONE]`.

tools.description: Functions the model may call (OpenAI function schema). When it calls one, the reply carries `choices[0].message.tool_calls` and `finish_reason: "tool_calls"`. Validated on `qwen3.6`.

reasoning_effort.description: How much the model reasons before answering. `none` turns reasoning off on every model in the catalogue except `glm5.3` and `glm5.3-flash`, which always reason: there `none` is applied as `minimal`. The other values deepen it: on `qwen3.6` and `gemma4` `low`, `medium`, `high` and `xhigh`/`max` cap the reasoning phase at 2,048 / 8,192 / 16,384 / 32,768 tokens; on `deepseek-v4-flash` and `qwen3.8-flash` they steer the depth; on `mimo-v2.6-flash` `minimal` is applied as `low` and `xhigh` as `max`. Without the parameter every model reasons. The reasoning trace arrives in `message.reasoning_content`. `thinking: {"type": "disabled"}`, `reasoning: {"enabled": false}`, `enable_thinking: false` and `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking: false` are accepted as aliases of `none`; this parameter wins over them. Details: [Controlling reasoning](https://nan.builders/docs/models#controlling-reasoning).

chat_template_kwargs.description: Accepted as an alias: `{ "enable_thinking": false }` means exactly `reasoning_effort: "none"`, on every model in the catalogue. Prefer `reasoning_effort`, which wins when both are sent. In OpenAI SDKs, pass it inside `extra_body`.

premium_tier.description: `glm5.3` is served only to keys on the GLM 5.3 premium tier. Same request shape as any other model, only `model` changes. A key without the tier gets `401` `auth_error`: "This API key does not have access to the requested model". It reads like a broken key and is not.

from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key="$NAN_API_KEY",
    base_url="https://api.nan.builders/v1",
)

# rerank isn't part of the OpenAI client, so call it directly:
resp = client.post(
    "/rerank",
    cast_to=object,
    body={
        "model": "rerank",
        "query": "What is the capital of France?",
        "documents": ["Paris is the capital of France.", "Berlin is the capital of Germany."],
    },
)

get.description:
The run's log, as a live stream or as JSON pages.

**Stream.** Send `Accept: text/event-stream` (with `curl`, add `-N`). The server first replays every stored event after your resume point, then sends new ones as they happen. Frames:

- `id: <seq>` + `event: run_event` + `data: <RunEvent>`: one event of the log.
- `event: state` + `data: {"state", "error_code"}`: the run changed state.
- `event: end` + `data: <Run>`: the run is over, or waiting for your approval (`awaiting_approval`), and every event has been sent. The server closes the stream after it.
- `: hb`: a comment line every 15 seconds that keeps the connection open. Ignore it.

To resume after a dropped connection, send the last `id` you received as the `Last-Event-ID` header (it wins over `after`): you get the rest without gaps or repeats. A stream lasts at most 30 minutes; if it closes before `end`, reconnect with `Last-Event-ID`. Up to 10 open streams per member (`429 too_many_streams`).

**JSON pages.** Without that `Accept` header the same endpoint answers one page of events after `after`. Pass the page's `next_after` as `after` until `done` is `true`.

post.description:
Starts a run of the automation now, with its saved instructions, secrets and approval settings: the same run a webhook or a schedule would start. Its agent proposes actions, which apply automatically or wait for your approval as the automation says. Follow it like any run (`GET /v1/runs/{id}/events`). Runs you start this way are never skipped by `skip_if_active` or cancelled by `supersede`, but they count towards the automation's `max_runs_per_hour` and the limits of every run.

Authentication: a member API key (`sk-...`) or a platform token (`nan_pat_...`) with the `automations:run` scope. Runs on NaN inference need a plan with inference; an automation that uses your own provider key needs an active workspace of yours instead. Any of these credentials may run an automation that uses your key: its instructions are fixed in the portal, and what you send as `input` reaches an agent that holds your key, so treat it as untrusted. Guide: [Use your own provider key](https://nan.builders/docs/runs#use-your-own-provider-key-byok).

apiKey.description: Member API key (`sk-...`), from "API Keys" in your settings on the platform. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <api-key>`. It works on every inference endpoint, on the Runs, Automations and Approvals endpoints and on the two Workspaces endpoints (it cannot approve runs or change automations). Personal and non-transferable. The key that lives inside a workspace (the one its agents use) is refused by the Runs endpoints with `403 workspace_key_not_allowed`.

platformToken.description: Platform token (`nan_pat_...`), from "Tokens" in your settings on the platform. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It works only on the platform API: Runs (`/v1/runs...`), Automations (`/v1/automations...`), Approvals, Secrets (`/v1/secrets...`), Notifications (`/v1/notification-channels...`) and the two Workspaces endpoints, and only where it carries the scope the endpoint names: `runs`, `workspaces:read`, `automations:read`, `automations:run`, `automations:write`, `secrets:read`, `secrets:write`, `notifications:read` or `notifications:write`. A missing scope answers `403 token_scope_denied`. New tokens get `runs` and `workspaces:read` by default; a token with an `automations:`, `secrets:` or `notifications:` scope can only be created from a browser sign-in. It never works for inference: inference endpoints refuse it with `401 token_not_valid_for_inference`. It can never approve a run, and it changes automations, secrets or notification channels only with `automations:write`, `secrets:write` or `notifications:write`. Shown once when you create it; up to 10 active; expires after 30, 90 or 365 days, or never; revocable at any time. Any member with an active subscription can create one; creating runs still needs a plan with inference.

cliSession.description: The session the [NaN CLI](https://nan.builders/docs/nan-cli) saves when you sign in with `nan auth login`, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <session>`. It manages your secrets, automations and notification channels where the write API is available for your account, and it can do everything you can do signed in, except approve. Sign in on your own machine: a session saved inside a workspace can be read by the agents that run there.

parameters.description: The parameters the function accepts, described as a JSON Schema object. When present, its root must be `"type": "object"`: a root of any other type, or with no `type`, is rejected with a `400` before the request reaches the model, on every model. ResponseFormat.description:
Force structured output. What each mode guarantees:

- `json_object`: syntactically valid JSON only, NOT its shape. Describe the schema you want in the prompt. On `deepseek-v4-flash` on `api.nan.builders` the prompt must also contain the word JSON, otherwise `400`.
- `json_schema` with `strict: true`: the output is constrained to the schema (fields, types and required keys).

`json_schema` works on `qwen3.6` and `gemma4`. On `deepseek-v4-flash` it is accepted on non-streamed `/chat/completions` requests without `tools`: the answer is checked against your schema and, when it does not match, usually re-served by a provider that enforces it; an answer that could not be checked, or a miss the re-serve could not replace in time, is returned as is (validate it if your code depends on it). Other `json_schema` requests on `deepseek-v4-flash` depend on the host: on the enterprise base URL (see the overview) they are accepted; on `api.nan.builders` a request that streams, carries `tools`, goes to `/responses`, sets `n` above 1, or whose schema is over 16 KB, invalid or one the gateway will not validate (a `$ref` outside the schema, `$dynamicRef` or `$anchor`, a nested `$id`, or too large once its `$ref`s are inlined) is rejected with a `400` before it reaches the model, and `json_object` still works there. For output that follows a schema on `deepseek-v4-flash` in those requests, define one function tool whose `parameters` is your JSON Schema (root `type: object`, `strict: true`), force it with `tool_choice: {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "..."}}` and read `choices[0].message.tool_calls[0].function.arguments`.

next_cursor.description: Pass it as `cursor` for the next page. `null` on the last page.

cwd.description: Where the agent works (inside the worktree when there is one).

worktree.description: The separate worktree, or `null` when the agent works in the folder.

branch.description: `nan-run/...` when there is a worktree, otherwise `null`.

checkout.description: Only on runs with a fresh checkout: the commit checked out.

RunEventDataLog.description: `data` of a `log` event. A line of output that is not a message.

RunEventDataMessage.description: `data` of a `message` event. Assistant text, sent incrementally: each event carries only its own chunk, and the last chunk of a message has `final: true` (its text may be empty). Concatenate the chunks to rebuild the message.

text.description: This chunk only, up to 16 KiB.

RunEventDataToolCall.description: `data` of a `tool_call` event. The agent called a tool.

RunEventDataToolResult.description: `data` of a `tool_result` event. What a tool answered. `id` matches its `tool_call`.

RunEventDataUsage.description: `data` of a `usage` event. Tokens used so far, as the agent reports them (cumulative).

RunEventDataError.description: `data` of an `error` event. Something went wrong.

RunEventDataTruncated.description: `data` of a `truncated` event. The run hit its event limit (20000 events) or size limit (16 MiB): later events are dropped, except `artifact`, `error` and `finished`.

RunEventDataFinished.description: `data` of a `finished` event. The run ended. Always the last event.

RunEvent.description: One event of a run's log. `type` says what `data` holds. Everything in `data` comes from the agent inside your workspace: treat it as untrusted text, never as markup. Secrets from the workspace's environment file are masked as `***`.

seq.description: 1, 2, 3... in order, per run. Use it to resume (`after`, `Last-Event-ID`).

type.description:
- `started`: The run started.
- `log`: A line of output that is not a message.
- `message`: Assistant text, sent incrementally: each event carries only its own chunk, and the last chunk of a message has `final: true` (its text may be empty). Concatenate the chunks to rebuild the message.
- `tool_call`: The agent called a tool.
- `tool_result`: What a tool answered. `id` matches its `tool_call`.
- `usage`: Tokens used so far, as the agent reports them (cumulative).
- `artifact`: A file the agent left in `artifacts/`.
- `error`: Something went wrong.
- `truncated`: The run hit its event limit (20000 events) or size limit (16 MiB): later events are dropped, except `artifact`, `error` and `finished`.
- `finished`: The run ended. Always the last event.
- `approval_required`: An automation run proposed actions that wait for your approval.
- `action`: One step of an `apply` run.

next_after.description: The last `seq` returned (or your `after` when the page is empty). Pass it as `after` for the next page.

done.description: `true` when the run is over and every event has been returned.

WorkspaceSlot.description: The purchased slot paying for the workspace.

Workspace.description: One of your workspaces. Never carries keys, environment values or agent configuration.

workspace_uuid.description: The workspace id. Accepted by `workspace` in `POST /v1/runs`.

name.description: Unique among your workspaces. Accepted by `workspace` in `POST /v1/runs`.

agent_selection.description: Agents and tools chosen for the workspace.

run_agents.description: The agents a run or an automation can use in this workspace, in display order (`pi`, `pi_gentle`, `hermes`). `pi` needs Pi installed, `pi_gentle` needs Pi and gentle-shell, `hermes` needs Hermes chosen for the workspace or installed. status.description: Runs can only be created while it is `running`.

ssh_command.description: The command to connect over SSH.

tier.description: Size. `free` is the Micro-sized workspace included with Premium.

state_reason.description: Why the workspace is not running normally, or `null`.

grace_until.description: When an open grace period ends (the data is deleted then), or `null`.

inference_attached.description: Whether the workspace has an inference key (never the key itself). Runs need it.

rescue.description: Rescue sessions during a grace period.

stale.description: `true` when the last snapshot is older than expected.

env_var_keys.description: Names of the variables in the workspace's environment file. Never the values.

event.description: The event name, for a webhook.

delivery.description: The delivery id, for a webhook.

payload.description: The input itself: a JSON object.

commit_message.description: `git_push`: the message of the pushed commit.

number.description: The pull request or issue number.

body.description: The text of a pull request, comment or review.

truncated.description: Only the first files are listed.

base.description: With a push: the base branch.

merge_base.description: With a push: the commit the pushed commit is built on.

state.description: `auto`: no action needed approval, they applied automatically. `pending`: waiting for you. `approved`, `rejected`, `expired`: what happened to it. `cancelled`: dropped without a decision (the automatic actions before it failed, the run was cancelled, or your membership no longer includes runs).

proposal_sha256.description: The hash of the stored proposal. Approving in the portal binds to it.

prefix_apply_run_id.description: The `apply` run of the actions before `approval_from`.

apply_run_id.description: The `apply` run of the approved actions.

next_cursor.description: Pass it as `cursor` for the next page. `null` on the last page.

updated_by.description: The kind of credential that made the last change: `browser_session` (the portal), `cli_session` (the NaN CLI after `nan auth login`) or `platform_token` (a `nan_pat_...` token). Objects last changed before the write API read `browser_session`.

attempt.description: The attempt number of this send (0 for a drop).

NotificationChannelCreated.description: The new channel, plus its signing secret for `https` channels: returned only here and by the rotation. Store it now.

name.description: Unique among your channels, without regard to case.

url_hint.description: The URL's host, then `/…/` and the last 4 characters of its path when the path is at least 20 bytes and they are letters, digits, `_` or `-`; the host alone otherwise. Never the URL.

disabled_reason.description: `member`: you disabled it. `failing`: 20 failed attempts in a row. `invalid_url`: the URL resolved to a refused address when sending. `null` while enabled.

signing.description: On `https` channels only (`null` otherwise): when the previous signing secret stops signing after a rotation (`null` when there is none).

updated_by.description: The credential of the last change.

signing_secret.description: `nan_nsec_` and 43 base64url characters. Only for `https` channels (absent otherwise). Never shown again.

BadRequest.description: Invalid parameter. The body includes `param` with the offending field. Safety filter returns `content_policy_violation`. A request that does not fit the model's context window also answers `400`. On `qwen3.6` and `gemma4` the message is "Context length exceeded for model '...'" with the model's limit; on the other models it is usually that text, but it can be the generic "Invalid request. Check your request parameters.". It is not retried automatically: shorten the input or pick a model with a larger window. A `max_tokens` above what the model can generate also answers a generic `400`.

Forbidden.description: Your tier lacks access to this endpoint (`tier_restricted`). Image generation requires `inference` membership.

RateLimited.description: Rate limit exceeded: `rpm_limit` or `max_parallel_requests` (`rate_limit_exceeded`), or monthly quota exhausted (`quota_exceeded` / `insufficient_quota`).

PaymentRequired.description: The token allowance for the billing period is spent on a model that carries one, such as `glm5.3`. The request was refused before it reached the model, so nothing ran. Not retryable: the counter returns to zero when your billing period starts. The wire `code` is `cap_reached` or `monthly_cap_reached`.

error.message: Token allowance for this billing period exhausted for model glm5.3. The counter returns to zero when your next billing period starts.

RunsUnauthorized.description: Missing or invalid credentials: no `Authorization` header, an unknown or revoked API key or platform token, or an expired one (`invalid_api_key`). The message may vary.

error.message: Invalid authentication credentials. Provide a valid NaN API key in the Authorization header.
